newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE robusta coffee ends up, fails to chase NY.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE robusta coffee ends up, fails to chase NY.

text.p: London robusta coffee futures, failing to chase soaring New York values, retraced further from their highs by the close on Wednesday on scale-up origin selling.
"It's entirely different circumtances," said one trader. While some London players are closing their books ahead of the month end, New York operators may have some more buying to be done.
"Furthermore, there's not much industry buying interest in robusta," the trader said.
London's benchmark stood $60 higher at $1,627 a tonne by the close after ranging from between $1,675 and $1,610.
A burst of fund and local buying provided much of the support in the morning and origin offers pared most of the gains.
New York's May arabica futures, extending overnight gains, marched to a high of 189 cents a lb in late morning trade on speculative buying.
Volume in London totalled just 5,281 lots.
Technically, May faces a layer of resistance starting from $1,700 and support is pegged at $1,600.
The London market had corrected higher on Tuesday afternoon after experiencing heavy losses since Monday on a fund sell-off.

Traders however said this morning's climb was also probably a bit overdone for now. Roasters who panicked after the sharply higher call this morning now appeared more relaxed and held back some buying.

In other news, Asian traders said Indonesia's coffee exports could come down by 10-20 percent this year to around 260,000-280,000 tonnes because of heavy rains and winds which pounded its coffee farms. Indonesia is the world's top robusta grower.
